title: cost: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Context:
This PR consolidates three related pieces of work to make cost-optimization automatic and safe for production workloads: 1) sensible defaults and autotune hooks for batching and KV-prefix caching, 2) curated quantization profiles (4/5/8-bit tuned per-instance) with runtime selection, and 3) unit-economics tooling (CLI + dashboard metrics + export) to let SREs and product teams understand per-route cost impact. Motivation: many customers ship with suboptimal batching/caching settings and conservative quant profiles. The goal is to reduce per-token cost by default while preserving tail latency and quality guarantees, and to give operators visibility and rollback controls.

What this changes (high-level):
- Introduces an autotune controller that samples traffic and proposes batch_size, max_latency_ms, and cache_ttl defaults per route. The controller runs asynchronously and emits recommended settings as suggestions in the console and as optional automatic rollouts.
- Adds runtime hooks for switching quantization profiles. We now ship three curated profiles: "q4_eco", "q5_balanced", and "q8_compat" with validation metadata (eval suites, expected token error bounds). The runtime will pick a fallback profile when hardware/latency constraints require it.
- Exposes unit-econ metrics: tokens_processed, tokens_cost_estimate, batch_efficiency, cache_hit_rate, and per-route projected_monthly_cost. Adds an export endpoint for one-click CSV reports for FinOps.
- Console changes: UI shows recommended defaults, confidence score, and an A/B canary toggle to stage recommendations.
- CLI: new `redwood autotune status|apply|rollback` commands for operators.

Implementation notes:
- Autotune runs as part of the runtime control plane. Recommendations are persisted to the config store with a lightweight change history for audit. Rollouts default to manual except for low-risk routes (low qps and high confidence).
- Quant profiles were generated from offline calibration runs (see scripts in tools/quant-profiles/) and validated against the full internal eval harness (perf + quality). Each profile includes a small validation set and expected latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Unit-econ tooling computes costs using current cloud pricing + model tokenization heuristics and is pluggable to customer pricing overrides.

Testing & Validation:
- Unit tests added for controller heuristics and serialization.
- Integration tests: simulated traffic runs show median per-token cost improvements of ~27% on sample workloads when using recommended settings; tail latency (p95) remained within SLA for 94% of routes in the canary dataset.
- Load tests: new canary job added to perf-canary to validate rollout safety before full apply.

Rollout plan:
1. Enable recommendations in the Console as suggestions (default off for auto-apply).
2. Run a 2-week canary across 10% of customers with auto-apply disabled but with one-click apply for each tenant.
3. After successful canary and signoff from SRE, enable auto-apply for low-risk routes with opt-out.

Backward compatibility and safety:
- All changes are opt-in; runtime always supports explicit per-route overrides.
- Rollback endpoints implemented; recommendations are reversible.
- Added conservative safety checks before switching quant profiles (quality delta threshold, latency SLO checks).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] CLI docs
- [x] Console UI prototype
- [x] Perf canary job

Related work:
- See ENG-2419 (autotune controller design) and ENG-2433 (quant profile generation).

Notes for reviewers: focus review on controller heuristics (autotune/controller.py) and the runtime quant switching (runtime/quant_profiles.py). The UI and CLI are intentionally small surface changes; most behavioral logic lives in the controller and runtime.

Commits summary:
- initial: add autotune controller, basic recommendation storage
- add: quant profile generation scripts + profile artifacts (calibration vectors small sample)
- add: runtime support for profile switching and compatibility checks
- add: unit-econ metrics and export endpoint
- docs: CLI + console help text
- tests: unit and integration tests
